identity_notes: Açaí berry human evidence is almost entirely small (n=10-55), short-duration acute or pilot trials measuring antioxidant/inflammatory biomarkers, oxidative-stress markers, or acute vascular/exercise-performance outcomes rather than hard clinical endpoints; results are consistently mixed, with the same trial often showing a positive secondary biomarker alongside a null primary or comparator-matched outcome. The single most important applicability caveat: many of the 'açaí' products tested are NOT isolated açaí — they are multi-fruit branded juice blends (MonaVie Active, açaí+camu-camu+blackberry juice), açaí-juçara fruit blends (a related but distinct Euterpe species), or açaí added on top of another active background intervention (hypoenergetic diet, calorie-restricted diet plan) — so results frequently cannot be attributed to açaí alone. The largest and most rigorous synthesis in this set, a 2025 meta-analysis of 8 RCTs/411 participants (PMID 39960343), found NO significant effect of açaí on any standard lipid-panel measure (LDL-c, HDL-c, total cholesterol, triglycerides), directly tempering the positive HDL-c signal seen in two individual smaller trials (32349893, 36206152) also kept in this set.
